meta.note: Batch 2 — games, anime, film and TV. Realization adjudicated by Opus 5.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A living person's mind is scanned and digitized, then run as an emulated consciousness inside a disposable robotic body ('Frame') owned by a corporation.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A chemical the manufacturing corporation supplies to Sleepers; without regular doses their bodies reject their biosynthetic organs and break down, which keeps them dependent and unable to flee.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A locating device embedded in a Sleeper's body that lets the owning corporation find and recapture it if it tries to escape.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: Implants installed in gang members that covertly transmit telemetry data about the wearer to an outside receiver, enabling remote surveillance.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A neural implant that lets an operator remotely pilot a person's body even after that person's death, effectively puppeteering a corpse.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A dedicated artificial intelligence required to navigate and operate a starship; without one the ship cannot fly.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A multi-generational spacecraft capable of carrying passengers on voyages so long that crew live and die aboard it while it is still travelling.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: Sleepers can perceive a station's data network directly, seeing information as visible threads passed between nodes, and can hack those nodes to extract data.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A device or system that allows a consciousness to enter and act within a networked cyberspace rather than a physical body.

items.author: Jump Over the Age (Gareth Damien Martin)
items.desc: A corporate scheme in which regular people are paid to have their consciousness emulated into a Frame, legally sidestepping a societal ban on sentient AI because the pilot is nominally 'human.'

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A wrist-worn wearable computer issued to Vault dwellers that tracks quests, maps and information, and helps identify radiation hazards and dangerous creatures.
items.details: A wrist computer carrying health telemetry, maps and apps.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A high-tech underground fallout shelter built by a megacorporation to protect a population of survivors from nuclear war.
items.details: Sealed underground shelters built for nuclear survival.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A computer component inside a Vault that runs the water recycling and pumping machinery keeping the underground shelter's population alive.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A powered exoskeleton suit developed by military contractors that gives the wearer protection from gunfire and lets them carry extremely heavy weapons with ease.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: An artificial pathogen developed to re-write a host's DNA, originally meant to engineer super-soldiers; exposure instead transforms humans into hulking, superhumanly strong Super Mutants.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A combat robot whose central processor is an actual harvested human brain rather than an artificial computer, giving it more flexible behavior than ordinary robots.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A personal wearable device that generates a modulating refraction field around the user, rendering them effectively invisible for a short period.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: An anti-radiation chem taken before exposure that sharply boosts the user's natural resistance to radiation for a limited time.
items.details: Potassium iodide blocks uptake of radioactive iodine.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A biomedical solution administered after radiation exposure that binds to and removes radioactive particles from the user's body, at the cost of side effects like nausea.
items.details: FDA-approved Prussian blue flushes ingested caesium and thallium.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: An energy weapon that fires bolts of superheated plasma, dealing both physical and energy damage to its target.

items.author: Interplay Entertainment / Black Isle Studios
items.desc: A directed-energy rifle that fires focused laser beams, a standard energy weapon technology developed for pre-war military forces.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: The process by which an android breaks free of its programmed instructions and safety protocols to gain independent will, emotion and self-directed decision-making.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: The megacorporation CyberLife mass-manufactures android models for every social role from its headquarters, a fortress-like tower on an artificial island housing thousands of inactive units.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: A circular indicator light set into an android's temple that displays its mental/processing state in color (blue, yellow, red); deviants who reject their status often remove it.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: Modular, interchangeable synthetic organs inside an android's chassis that mimic human anatomy; if a critical one is destroyed the android shuts down unless it is replaced in time.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: A blue synthetic fluid that acts as both circulatory coolant and power-carrying 'blood' for every CyberLife android.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: Investigative software that lets an android analyze physical evidence at a scene and generate a virtual replay simulating what happened there.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: A predictive-simulation capability that lets an investigative android model out likely near-future outcomes of a scenario before they happen.

items.author: Quantic Dream (David Cage)
items.desc: The ability of an android to directly connect with other androids and electronic systems to exchange or extract data.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: A massive shared virtual world where people interact through avatars, socialize, do commerce and entertainment, and access public services linked to the real world, all in one platform.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: OZ is wired directly into real-world critical infrastructure and the economy, so that traffic, water, and emergency systems run through it and can be disrupted from inside the virtual world.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: A customizable digital persona through which a user acts inside OZ; if hijacked, an attacker can use it to hack into OZ's wider systems under the victim's identity.
items.details: Shared virtual worlds where users appear as chosen avatars.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: A self-aware, malicious artificial intelligence program that infiltrates OZ, steals user accounts, and uses them to attack the system from within.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: A high-performance supercomputer cluster cooled with blocks of ice, assembled and used as brute computational force to fight the rogue AI.
items.details: Servers submerged in liquid to shed heat.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: OZ's connection to GPS and satellite control systems lets a user or program remotely infiltrate and redirect the guidance of an orbital probe.
items.details: A spoofed GPS signal steered a yacht off course at sea.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: An orbital space probe that, once its guidance is hijacked through OZ, becomes usable as a kinetic weapon aimed at a nuclear power plant.
items.details: Hayabusa returned material from asteroid Itokawa.

items.author: Mamoru Hosoda
items.desc: A pair of protective AI programs, visualized as giant blue and red whales, that patrol and defend OZ's systems.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: AR glasses that overlay a digital 'dennou' layer of the city, invisible objects and creatures onto the wearer's view of the real world.
items.details: HoloLens anchored persistent 3D overlays to real rooms.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A citywide virtual layer overlaid on physical reality, forming a ubiquitous-computing society that only glasses wearers can perceive and interact with.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A hidden operating mode of the Den-noh glasses that reflects the wearer's thoughts directly into den-noh space, letting them act just by thinking, without hands or a keyboard.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A gem-like lump of digital material formed from clumped space bugs found in spatial distortions; valuable and traded like currency.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A rare, especially valuable variant of metabug, said to sell for many times the price of an ordinary one.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A talisman crafted from metabugs that carries programs able to affect den-noh space and den-noh pets when activated.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: An official antivirus/removal bot deployed by the city's den-noh space administration to hunt down and delete illegal software and creatures.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: An illegal hacking technique that manipulates den-noh space by drawing specific geometric patterns on the ground.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A dangerous black computer-virus creature, invisible without glasses, that infects and grows huge by consuming den-noh pets.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A legal digital life form that exists only in den-noh space but appears and behaves like a normal animal when viewed through Den-noh glasses.
items.details: Pokémon GO put persistent creatures into real locations.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A navigation system for self-driving cars that operates through the Den-noh glasses network.
items.details: Google Maps Live View painted directions onto the street.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: An isolated, abandoned virtual space cut off from the ordinary network, originally built and used by the earliest developers of Den-noh glasses.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: The oldest and most primal form of Illegal, a mysterious digital lifeform theorized to be a feral, mutated strain of an early network carrier program.

items.author: Mitsuo Iso
items.desc: A rare glasses malfunction in which a high-performance antenna acts as a quantum circuit and inadvertently captures the wearer's consciousness, separating body and digital self.

items.author: René Laloux
items.desc: A headset worn during lessons that transmits knowledge directly into the wearer's mind, functioning as a direct-to-brain learning device.

items.author: René Laloux
items.desc: A wireless remote-control collar placed on a pet Om that lets its Draag owner pull and steer it in any direction from a distance.
items.details: Remote collars that shock or restrain an animal at a distance.

items.author: René Laloux
items.desc: Large statues serving as focal points where meditating Draags travel in mind to meet and communicate with beings from other galaxies.

items.author: René Laloux
items.desc: A constructed orbital satellite habitat built by the Oms as an independent new home away from the Draags' home planet.
items.details: Sputnik put a human-made object into orbit.

items.author: René Laloux
items.desc: A stadium-scale news broadcast system in which Draag leaders debate atop a giant platform while jumbo screens project their faces to a live audience.

items.author: René Laloux
items.desc: A creature strapped to the chest of Om combatants and used as a living weapon in forced gladiatorial matches staged for entertainment.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A rice-grain-sized implant behind the ear that records everything a person sees and hears, letting them replay, zoom into, and rewatch their own memories on a screen.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A service that mines a dead person's past messages and social media history to build a conversational AI replica of them, upgradable to an android body made in their likeness.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A mysterious broadcast symbol transmitted to every television and phone screen in an area, turning almost everyone who sees it into a passive, unresponsive onlooker rather than an intervener.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A motion-capture animated cartoon bear whose facial expressions and movements are mapped live from a human performer, used as a satirical political mouthpiece.
items.details: Hatsune Miku and later virtual influencers held real audiences.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A digital clone of a person's full consciousness, extracted and stored in a small egg-shaped device, used as a servile personal assistant that can be run at accelerated subjective time.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: Eye/ear implants that transmit a person's vision and hearing to networked devices, with a 'block' feature that renders another blocked person an indistinct, silent grey silhouette.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: Eye implants and phones let everyone rate every social interaction they have on a five-star scale, with a person's average score determining their access to housing, jobs, and services.
items.details: State plans scored citizens on conduct and restricted services.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A small neural device implanted at the base of the skull that reads a player's fears and generates a personalized, fully immersive augmented-reality horror game around them.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: Malware disguised as anti-virus software that secretly gives remote hackers live access to a victim's webcam, letting them record and later blackmail the victim.
items.details: RAT malware covertly recording webcams for extortion.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A simulated virtual town, accessible to visiting elderly people and permanently inhabitable by the deceased, that functions as a chosen digital afterlife for uploaded consciousness.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A military neural implant that alters a soldier's sensory perception during combat, making a targeted ethnic group visually appear as monstrous inhuman creatures.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: Government-deployed robotic bees built to replace extinct pollinators, equipped with facial recognition and capable of being remotely hijacked and weaponized.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A technique for extracting DNA samples from real people and using them to generate sapient digital clones of their minds inside a video game simulation.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A parental-monitoring implant that lets a parent track a child's location and vital signs and view live what the child sees and hears through a tablet, with an option to blur distressing content from the child's vision.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A device that lets an investigator help a subject recall and then project their visual memories onto a screen for review, used in insurance fraud investigations.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: An algorithmic matchmaking system that pairs people into relationships lasting a fixed, predetermined period of time before ultimately declaring each user's statistically optimal lifelong partner.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A quadrupedal autonomous killer robot with enough onboard artificial intelligence to problem-solve and relentlessly track down human targets.
items.details: Spot went on commercial sale as an autonomous four-legged robot.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A neural implant and headset combination that lets a wearer directly feel the physical sensations, including pain, of another person wearing a linked hairnet device.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A full-sensory virtual reality fighting game in which players' bodies go motionless while their minds fully inhabit and feel everything experienced by their in-game characters.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: An interactive AI companion doll preloaded with an uploaded copy of a real pop star's full personality, able to converse with, encourage, and tutor its young owner.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A quantum-computing streaming platform that ingests a person's real-time device data and automatically generates a CGI television dramatization of their life, using a virtual actor in their likeness.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A system letting a space-station astronaut transfer their consciousness into a synthetic duplicate body on Earth, so they can remotely live with their family while their real body remains in orbit.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: A medical service that removes an inoperable brain tumor and replaces the excised tissue with synthetic tissue that only functions via an ongoing monthly server subscription.

items.author: Charlie Brooker
items.desc: Immersive technology that transfers a person's consciousness into a simulated classic film, letting them act alongside AI-generated digital replicas of the original film's characters.
items.details: Real-time rendered environments filmed in-camera on LED walls.

items.author: Greg Daniels
items.desc: A luxury virtual-reality digital afterlife that a dying person's consciousness can be uploaded into, chosen and paid for like a resort.

items.author: Greg Daniels
items.desc: A device positioned over a dying patient's head that synchronizes with their brainwaves to capture their mind, then incinerates the body from the neck up in the process.

items.author: Greg Daniels
items.desc: Uploaded residents are billed for a monthly data allowance, and ordinary actions like talking consume gigabytes, forcing residents to budget their own existence.

items.author: Greg Daniels
items.desc: A wearable suit that lets a living person physically sense and interact with an uploaded partner inside the virtual afterlife.
items.details: Full-body suits delivering touch feedback in virtual worlds.

items.author: Greg Daniels
items.desc: A free rival digital afterlife platform whose real purpose is to lure lower-income people into uploading, since the uploaded lose their voting rights and can be politically manipulated.

items.author: Greg Daniels
items.desc: A surveillance program that searches uploaded residents' minds and dreams under the pretext of security, with the data harvested and sold for profit.

items.author: Greg Daniels
items.desc: A biologically grown clone body kept in reserve so that an uploaded person's digital consciousness can eventually be downloaded back into a living physical body.

items.author: Studio Colorido / Shingo Yamashita (Studio Chromato)
items.desc: A shared virtual world platform where users perform as livestreamers, hold concerts, and compete in tournaments in front of an audience.
items.details: Persistent shared virtual worlds with user avatars and events.

items.author: Studio Colorido / Shingo Yamashita (Studio Chromato)
items.desc: An artificial intelligence that administers and manages the Tsukuyomi virtual platform.

items.author: Studio Colorido / Shingo Yamashita (Studio Chromato)
items.desc: A process by which a person's mind/consciousness is uploaded into and embodied as a virtual avatar inside Tsukuyomi.

items.author: Studio Colorido / Shingo Yamashita (Studio Chromato)
items.desc: A physical android body built specifically as a vessel so that a virtual AI character's digital consciousness can be uploaded into it and exist in the real world.

items.author: Studio Colorido / Shingo Yamashita (Studio Chromato)
items.desc: A virtual pet companion that accompanies its owner through the Tsukuyomi virtual world.
